At JetBrains, code is our passion. Ever since we started, back in 2000, we have strived to make the strongest, most effective developer tools on earth. By automating routine checks and corrections, our tools speed up production, freeing developers to grow, discover, and create.
ThinkRail is an innovative project within JetBrains' Innovation Hub. Its aim is to develop a declarative programming language tailored to AI-spec-driven development. Our goal is to build an infrastructure that enables the efficient creation of complex systems with AI, while maintaining the trust of users and flexibility in the results.
Thinkrail is now open source and in alpha, and we’re entering the next stage of the product’s development: initial market penetration. We’re focused on bringing it into real-world projects and turning it into a robust, production-ready system. To help us get there, we’re looking for a software developer to join the team. Care about building trust in AI.
Love programming languages.

Build and evolve VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA plugins for ThinkRail.
Develop our language server, including analysis, completion, diagnostics, and verification.
Improve the evaluator that turns specs into code and catches spec and code drift.
Integrate ThinkRail with AI agent frameworks (e.g. Koog, LangGraph, and Spring AI) and protocols like MCP and ACP.

At Jumio , the Software Development Engineer IV - QA (SDE-IV, QA) is a senior technical role focused on ensuring the quality, performance, and reliability of highly scalable web portals and distributed backend systems. Our platform spans multiple Java Spring Boot microservices and customer-facing web portals , deployed across AWS ECS, EKS, and Lambda , and integrated through event-driven messaging using SNS/SQS .
In this role you will design and drive the test automation strategy for both UI (Playwright) and API/service layers, set the quality bar for the team, and act as a force multiplier — mentoring other engineers and embedding quality earlier in the development lifecycle. You will work closely with development, product, and DevOps teams to ensure our products meet the highest standards of quality, scalability, and security.
This is a hands-on senior IC role: you will write code, but you will also influence architecture, own cross-service test strategy, and make build-vs-buy decisions for testing tooling.
T-Shaped Engineering Expectation
As part of Jumio 's engineering culture, you will adopt a T-shaped engineering approach. Beyond deep expertise in test automation and quality engineering, you will contribute across the development lifecycle — understanding software architecture, participating in design and API-contract discussions, reviewing application code, and ensuring our distributed systems are testable, observable, and resilient by design.
Role Value
This role is critical to ensuring the reliability, scalability, and security of Jumio 's products. By architecting and maintaining automated testing frameworks across web, API, and event-driven layers, you will enable faster, higher-confidence releases and reduce production risk in a complex microservices environment.

Test Architecture & Strategy
Define and own the end-to-end automated test strategy across web portals and backend microservices, balancing UI, API, contract, integration, and end-to-end coverage (test pyramid).
Design test strategies for distributed, event-driven systems — including asynchronous flows through SNS/SQS , eventual consistency, idempotency, message ordering, retries, and dead-letter handling.
Automation Engineering
Develop and maintain robust test automation frameworks for web ( Playwright , Selenium, or equivalent) and API testing, using Java and/or JavaScript/TypeScript .
Automate API and service-level testing (REST/JSON, and async messaging) to validate functionality, performance, and resilience.
Build maintainable, scalable framework abstractions (page objects, fixtures, data builders, reusable test harnesses) that other engineers adopt.
Cloud-Native & Non-Functional Testing
Design tests that run against services deployed on ECS, EKS, and Lambda , including environment provisioning and teardown.
Use tools like TestContainers / LocalStack to test AWS integrations (SQS/SNS, Lambda, etc.) reliably and locally.
Drive performance, load, and resilience testing (e.g., JMeter, k6, Gatling, Locust) for highly scalable services, and partner with engineering on results and bottlenecks.
Contribute to non-functional quality: basic security testing, reliability, and chaos/failure-injection where appropriate.
CI/CD & Quality Engineering
Integrate automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions / Jenkins / GitLab CI) to enable fast feedback and continuous delivery.
Improve test reliability — reduce flakiness, optimize execution time, enable parallelization, and improve observability of test results.
Define and track quality metrics (coverage, escape rate, MTTR, flake rate) and use them to drive decisions.
AI-Augmented Engineering
Leverage LLM-based tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor) to accelerate test authoring, framework development, test-data generation, and debugging — driving measurable productivity and coverage gains.
Apply AI to quality engineering workflows: generating and maintaining test cases from requirements/specs, summarizing failures and triaging flaky tests, reviewing code, and scaffolding boilerplate so the team focuses on high-value testing.
Champion responsible, effective AI adoption within the QA team — establishing prompts, patterns, and guardrails, and mentoring engineers on using these tools to work faster without compromising rigor or correctness.
Collaboration & Leadership
Partner with developers to ensure comprehensive coverage and efficient issue resolution; review application and test code.
Mentor and uplevel SDE-II/III QA engineers on automation best practices, framework design, and testing strategy.
Influence design and architecture discussions to make systems more testable and to shift quality left.
Continuously evaluate and introduce new tools, methodologies, and best practices.

Strong programming skills in Java (Spring Boot ecosystem) and/or JavaScript/TypeScript .

The Mission Systems Software Engineer will work on developing solutions of a real time system environment to provide mission computing support at the center of an autonomous aircraft with sensor and weapons. This role will work to establish a software architecture for a real time system that operates in a multi-level environment at real time.

The role will require work with hardware, software and systems teams to come to a consensus design. This role will focus on development of new systems and software designs from PDR, CoDR, CDR to lab test, flight test and fielding.

Serve as a software mission systems engineer for a safety- and mission-critical real-time mission-computing system aligned with A-GRA and AMS-GRA principles, profiles, interfaces, and data standards.
Define and maintain the end-to-end software architecture, including mission applications, platform services, middleware, operating-system interfaces, hardware-abstraction layers, networking, data distribution, component boundaries, and APIs.
Architect for deterministic real-time performance by addressing scheduling, latency, jitter, synchronization, throughput, resource utilization, distributed processing, and CPU/GPU/accelerator allocation.
Develop architecture views, interface definitions, data-flow and deployment models, sequence and timing diagrams, resource budgets, trade studies, and technical decision records.
Integrate sensors, effectors, communications, navigation, autonomy, mission management, command-and-control, data-processing, and vehicle services in collaboration with hardware, FPGA, cybersecurity, safety, systems, integration, and test teams.
Design for mission resilience and assurance through fault detection and isolation, redundancy, graceful degradation, recovery, health monitoring, cybersecurity, airworthiness, certification, and requirements traceability.
Establish engineering practices for concurrency, synchronization, memory and resource management, deterministic execution, interface control, configuration management, and predictable component integration.
Define and execute verification strategies across HIL/SIL laboratories, simulations, test benches, flight-test environments, and deployed systems using automated, performance, stress, fault-injection, interface, and timing tests.
Maintain technical ownership throughout the system lifecycle by evaluating enabling technologies and supplier designs, analyzing performance, managing technical debt and modernization roadmaps, promoting reuse, and communicating architectural decisions.

Find the problems that are business critical, prioritize ruthlessly, and make the big tradeoff calls without slowing anyone down.
Build AI-platform and AI-native capabilities — the agent harness, agent building (custom agents and workflows), tool calling, retrieval, memory and context management, personalization and tone, the thread experience, and the evals that turn model quality into product quality.
Ship the systems that make Harvey work: retrieval over petabyte-scale document corpora, ingestion growing 10x every six months, data collection across 50+ jurisdictions, and government-level security for the world's most sensitive matters.
Ship across the stack — React and TypeScript alongside Python and Postgres — architecting intuitive UX and robust APIs for streaming results, long-running processes, and complex tool-calling workflows.
Mentor senior and staff engineers, and raise the bar for how the whole org builds.

Depth in full stack, backend, or agents/AI — and enough range to be useful outside it.
Experience building scalable, extensible systems that support multiple product lines.
Track record of shipping highly intuitive products in fast-growing SaaS, strong attention to detail.
Experience with React, TypeScript, CSS (we use TailwindCSS), Python, or related. For agents/AI, proficiency in Python plus hands-on work building and shipping agentic systems — agent harnesses/loops, tool use, memory, and evals — not just calling LLM APIs.
You embrace AI in how you build: AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or similar) are a core part of how you ship, and you have sharp instincts for where they accelerate work and where they fall short.
A history of influencing and aligning engineers and leaders well outside your direct scope.
Strong programming skills and general Computer Science knowledge.
Grit — experience working at early-stage startups is a plus.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join
The Quality Platform team is at the heart of Airbnb’s mission to deliver a seamless, high-quality experience for millions of hosts and guests. We don’t just find bugs — we build the systems that prevent them.
Our team sits at the intersection of Quality Engineering, Infrastructure, and Applied AI. We are evolving how software quality is built by integrating LLMs, intelligent automation, and data-driven systems into the testing lifecycle. You will join a high-impact group of engineers focused on building AI-powered quality systems that scale across one of the world’s most complex codebases.

As a Mobile Software Engineer, you will be a key contributor to the development of our Quality Platform across both native mobile stacks. You will help build the foundation for how quality is engineered across Airbnb's iOS and Android ecosystems, developing tools and frameworks that enable our mobile platform to scale while keeping developers productive and confident, regardless of which platform they build on.

Build AI-Driven Solutions: Contribute to AI-native agents that automate repetitive testing tasks and provide intelligent feedback to developers on both platforms.Deliver Scalable Infrastructure: Develop and maintain the high-scale platforms and testing environments used daily by the iOS and Android engineering organizations.Promote Engineering Craft: Implement best-in-class mobile patterns and modularity to improve testability and fault-tolerance across both native codebases.Contribute to Operational Excellence: Ensure our automated systems are performant and reliable, making data-driven decisions to optimize the CI/CD lifecycle for both platforms.
A Typical Day
Deliver Technical Excellence: Design and sustain foundational testing frameworks in Swift and Kotlin, emphasizing high performance and developer-centric reliability.
Deploy Intelligent Automation: Integrate LLM-powered solutions to drive autonomous test discovery and smart orchestration across our native mobile ecosystems.
Architect Quality by Design: Partner with cross-functional mobile teams to eliminate bottlenecks and ensure robust quality is integrated into the earliest stages of development.
Modernize Infrastructure: Scale distributed testing systems to optimize the CI/CD lifecycle, effectively reducing build latency for both iOS and Android stacks.
Drive R&D Initiatives: Work alongside Research and Data Science units to prototype next-generation tools that redefine software quality engineering.
Elevate Engineering Standards: Participate in deep-dive code reviews and the Quality Guild to advocate for best-in-class mobile patterns across the organization.
Your Expertise
Experience: Up to 4+ years of professional mobile development experience in a fast-paced, high-growth tech environment.
Technical Proficiency: Working knowledge of both Kotlin/Android SDK and Swift/iOS SDK, with experience using modern build tools (Gradle, Xcode).
Framework Development: Demonstrated experience building or extending test automation frameworks (e.g., Espresso, Compose Test, XCUITest) and mobile infrastructure.
Platform Mindset: A passion for building tools and SDKs that serve other engineers and improve the developer experience across platforms.
AI Curiosity: An eagerness to learn and apply AI/LLMs to solve complex engineering and quality challenges.
Execution & Ownership: Demonstrated ability to navigate complex codebases and take ownership of features or components from implementation to deployment.
Communication: Effective communication skills with the ability to collaborate across diverse technical and product teams.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative. Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.
Frontier AI runs on datacenters, and the world is in the middle of the largest infrastructure buildout in a generation. The binding constraint on progress is increasingly everything around the chips: land, power, permits, equipment, and the design and construction of the buildings themselves. Bringing a single site online involves hundreds of people, thousands of components, and decisions that move enormous amounts of capital. Much of that work still runs on spreadsheets and handoffs.
At Anthropic, we're building software and Claude-powered tools to help Anthropic scale out its compute, and we think there's an enormous opportunity to rethink how that work gets done. It's early, it's already having a real impact, and the engineers who join now will shape how one of the most consequential buildouts in the world gets done.
We're looking for strong, versatile software engineers who love building for people doing real work in the physical world. You'll embed with the teams that source sites, design buildings, procure equipment, and manage construction, learn their work deeply, and build the tools and systems they rely on every day. Datacenter experience is a big plus, but what matters most is that you can earn the trust of expert operators, model a messy domain cleanly, and move fast.

Build the core systems that track a datacenter's lifecycle (sites, designs, bills of materials, equipment, and construction progress) in one trusted, permissioned source of truth
Embed with datacenter, energy, and supply chain teams to understand how the work actually gets done, find the critical path, and build the tools they reach for first
Bring order to messy data by migrating and reconciling spreadsheets and legacy trackers, and integrate with the industry's tools, like construction management, scheduling, and engineering systems
Design for trust: fine-grained permissions, auditability, and data quality for information that steers major investment decisions
Ship early, iterate with users, and cut anything that doesn't help bring compute online sooner
Partner with research to understand new model capabilities and share where they fall short in engineering-heavy, physical-world domains
You may be a good fit if you
Have 8+ years of experience building software, with strong full-stack skills and solid grounding in data modeling, APIs, and databases
Have built software that teams in a physical-world industry depend on, such as datacenters, construction, energy, manufacturing, supply chain, or logistics
Have a track record of zero-to-one work in startup or startup-like environments
Are deeply user-centric: you learn the domain from the people doing the work and validate with them before over-investing
Bring high agency and good judgment about what matters, and hold strong opinions loosely
Communicate clearly across engineering, operations, and research, and care about the societal impacts of your work
Strong candidates may also have
Experience in datacenters (at a hyperscaler, colocation provider, operator, utility, or engineering firm), or in adjacent fields like construction, logistics, or legal
Experience with the domain's tooling, such as construction management (Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud), scheduling (Primavera P6), PLM/BOM, ERP and procurement, CAD/BIM, DCIM, or power system studies
A background in electrical, mechanical, or civil engineering, energy systems, or supply chain alongside a software career
Experience building products with large language models
Candidates need not have
100% of the skills listed above

Direct machine learning or AI research experience

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

The Safeguards ML Inference Path team designs, builds, and operates the production infrastructure that powers Claude's ML based safety systems. We collaborate closely with safety researchers and inference engineers to bring new classifiers and novel classes of ML defenses to production.

We own the research → production transfer of new safety technologies that is on the critical path for every Claude model launch. And we build for scale: serving thousands of ML classifiers, for all requests on the token generation path, and for every platform Claude runs on -- 1P, Bedrock, Vertex, and beyond.
We’re growing the team and looking for engineers who have deep expertise in productionizing ML systems. You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, large-scale distributed systems, and AI safety, developing the platforms and tools that enable our safeguards to operate reliably at scale. And your tooling and infrastructure will be used for every model launch, which are becoming more complex, and more frequent.

Design and build scalable ML infrastructure to support real-time safety deployments across our classifier and model ecosystem
Build monitoring and observability tools to track classifier performance, data quality, and system health for safety-critical applications
Collaborate with research teams to productionize safety research, translating experimental safety techniques into robust, scalable systems
Optimize inference latency and throughput for real-time safety evaluations while maintaining high reliability standards
Implement automated testing, deployment, and rollback systems for ML models in production safety applications
Partner with Safeguards, Security, and Alignment teams to understand requirements and deliver infrastructure that meets safety and production needs
Contribute to the development of internal tools and frameworks that accelerate safety research and deployment

Knowledge of privacy-preserving ML techniques and compliance requirements

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world’s toughest problems—from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world’s best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.
Genie One is building the AI coworker for business users: a trusted, governed way to ask questions of enterprise data, explore insights, and take action in the flow of work. Our team brings that experience to users wherever they are—across the web, mobile, and desktop applications—so a field employee, executive, or knowledge worker can move from question to insight without being constrained by a browser or a desk.
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Genie One Mobile & Desktop team, you will define and deliver the technical foundations for this multi-surface experience. You will work at the intersection of Web UI, Mobile, Desktop, shared frontend infrastructure, and enterprise-grade authentication and governance.

This is an opportunity to shape a product and an architecture that are still evolving rapidly: deciding what should be shared, what should be platform-specific, and how to keep the whole system coherent as new capabilities arrive.
The impact you will have
Set the technical direction for Genie One across web, native mobile, and desktop.
Lead the delivery of customer-facing experiences on iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows, balancing web feature parity with native capabilities such as notifications, background activity, multi-window workflows, deep links, and local-file interactions.
Shape and execute the long-term product and engineering strategy for Genie One Mobile & Desktop.
Build reusable cross-surface primitives, contracts, and patterns with shared product capabilities
Make the hybrid codebase easier to evolve by improving boundaries between web views, native shells, platform APIs, shared services, authentication, session management, and client-side state.
Raise the bar for quality and operational excellence for Mobile & Desktop: testing, release automation, telemetry, performance, security
Multiply team through technical leadership, mentoring, and hands-on contributions to the most important problems.
What we look for
8+ years of software engineering experience and a track record of shipping and operating customer-facing products at scale.
Staff-level technical leadership: setting direction across teams, making durable architecture decisions, and driving complex projects from definition through adoption.
A hybrid product background spanning web UI, mobile, desktop, or shared frontend platforms—with the ability to drive across all of them.
Strong experience with JavaScript or TypeScript and modern web frameworks such as React, plus hands-on experience with mobile or desktop application development.
The ability to navigate and improve a dynamic codebase spanning shared web code, React Native or native modules, desktop shells, webviews, backend APIs, and CI/CD.
Experience building secure, reliable products involving authentication, session management, enterprise networking, permissions, sensitive data, and enterprise device/application management such as Mobile Device Management (MDM) and Mobile Application Management (MAM).
A customer-focused, bias-to-action mindset and excellent communication skills. You make pragmatic trade-offs, learn quickly, and collaborate effectively across engineering, product, design, and security.
You do not need to be an expert in every framework or operating system. You do need to be comfortable working across layers and keeping interconnected web, mobile, and desktop experiences coherent as the product evolves.

Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.
Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

What We Do
Driving the plug-in power behind Unreal Engine 5. We bridge connections for licensees and our own internal game teams to online services. This allows games like Fortnite to utilize a combination of platform online services as well as Epic’s own online services to build cross-platform online features. Login, parties, voice chat, matchmaking, purchasing, cloud storage, and analytics are just a few examples of online features that our Online Game Services team helps games utilize.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer Intern to join us to continue to build the system that powers Fortnite. You'll work on the team responsible for things like running FNCS tournaments, storing player cosmetics and Sprites, and persisting LEGO Fortnite worlds. You will be given a feature to own as part of our development cycle, and be integrated in the day-to-day of the team.
In this role, you will
Contribute to the backend systems that power Fortnite experiences
Learn about security, scalability, and maintainability in the code you write
Collaborate with a team of highly experienced engineers
Work with Fortnite product owners and producers to figure out solutions that empower the upcoming seasons of Fortnite

Proficiency in Java or similar object-oriented programming language
Experience with AI-assisted coding tools, such as Claude code
Ability to communicate effectively and provide task updates in a remote-first team environment
Willingness to ask questions, seek guidance, and learn from feedback
Foundational analytical and problem-solving skills
Familiarity with cloud technologies, particularly AWS, is preferred
Familiarity with *nix based systems is a plus

We're transforming the grocery industry
At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community.

We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.
Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
Instacart is a Flex First team
There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Carrot Ads is Instacart's publisher advertising platform and one of its fastest-growing businesses. We power ads for enterprise retail partners like Uber Eats, Hy-Vee, and Thrive Market on their own storefronts, spanning Storefront, Storefront Pro, and the Connect / Carrot Ads API. As the first vertical team inside a historically horizontal Ads org, our scope is unusually broad: we own the publisher customer end to end while building on top of shared serving, measurement, and quality systems.
Retail media is consolidating, and Instacart is positioned to win on cross-retailer reach. Our goal is to become the premier grocery ads ecosystem for partners and advertisers — and getting there means turning an early externalization into an enterprise-grade platform that the world's most sophisticated retailers trust with their own storefronts. That is the problem you will help solve.
As a Software Engineer II on Carrot Ads, you will independently build and ship features across the publisher-facing stack: the Connect / Carrot Ads API, publisher serving inputs, reporting, and the tooling partners use to run their ad businesses.

You will write efficient, observable, well-tested code, own what you ship through production and on-call, and work as an away team into shared systems when a feature needs changes there. This is a high-visibility role inside one of Instacart's top growth areas, with real opportunity to own meaningful surfaces early in your career here.

Build and ship publisher-facing features end to end across Storefront, Storefront Pro, and API partners — including API endpoints, serving inputs, reporting views, and configuration tooling that partners depend on daily.
Extend the Connect / Carrot Ads API with clear contracts, robust event handling and dead-letter recovery, integration tests, and self-serve documentation that makes partner onboarding faster and more reliable.
Build the retailer control surface: relevance and quality-score inputs, reserve pricing, ad-load controls, and the trade-off signals retailers use to tune performance on their own sites.
Strengthen reporting and data integrity across partner systems — including attribution, catalog and product-ID mapping, reconciliation, and automated health checks that keep partner data trustworthy.
Raise reliability by helping define and meet partner SLAs, improving observability, reducing incident frequency and time to recovery, and contributing to a unified partner-health monitoring layer.
Debug partner-facing serving and reporting issues, tracing root causes across shared serving, measurement, and quality systems.
Collaborate across Product, Enterprise Solutions, and the horizontal Ads teams — including Serving, Measurement, Ads Quality, and Ads Manager — to land work that spans multiple stacks.
Use AI-assisted developer tools to move faster without lowering the bar on quality or security.
You work well in ambiguity, like owning features end to end, and want the surface area of a fast-growing business alongside the depth of hard systems problems.

3+ years of experience building and operating production backend services.
Strong API design and distributed-systems fundamentals, with fluency in a backend language such as Go, Ruby, or Python.
Demonstrated track record of shipping features end to end with solid testing, observability, and operational ownership.
Experience debugging across service boundaries and collaborating across cross-functional teams.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience in ad tech, retail media, or other publisher- or partner-facing platforms.
Familiarity with event streaming and reliability patterns at scale (e.g., Kafka, dead-letter queues, idempotent processing).
Cloud infrastructure experience with AWS or GCP, including data or measurement-adjacent systems.
Experience with data reconciliation, attribution, or catalog and entity mapping.
Experience building partner- or customer-facing APIs, including documentation, error contracts, and integration test coverage.

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to join our Road Safety & Telematics team. At Lyft, Telematics data is used to make Lyft safer by reducing the frequency and severity of accidents, which in turn also makes Lyft more affordable for riders and a better way to earn a living for drivers.

The Telematics team acts as a platform team that processes petabytes of mobile sensor data — millisecond-level IMU, gyroscope, and GPS signals — through a series of DAG-based transformations and ML model inferences to detect harsh driving events and convert them into normalized risk features that other Lyft services consume.
Our technology stack runs on AWS, Kubernetes, Spark, and Apache Airflow.

In this role, you'll work closely with data scientists, actuarial teams, other backend and data engineers, and product management — partnering across geos to build risk-aware products that rank and reward safe drivers, help off-board unsafe ones, notify drivers in real time, and give claims agents the tools to understand exactly what happened in a ride.

You'll also be a key technical partner to our insurance team as they optimize coverage costs and provider relationships.
If you are a seasoned engineer with a passion for innovation, high-volume data pipelines, microservices, working in cross-disciplinary environments and possess the skills to ensure the ongoing maintenance and improvement of services, you will thrive on our team!
You can read about some of the products that Telematics powers in this blog post: https://www.lyft.com/blog/posts/lyfts-impact-on-road-safety

Be a champion of the team's safety and affordability mission, serving as a reliable source of risk insights for teams across Lyft — from driver ranking and safety rewards to accident claims resolution and insurance strategy.
Lead medium to large projects, ensuring end-to-end execution with a focus on high quality and reliability.
Work cross-functionally with Data Scientists to productionize models that turn raw sensor signals into harsh-event detection and risk features, driving the team's industry-leading innovation in this space.
Drive future work to reduce latency, simplify, and improve the accuracy of both our back-end and on-device models that predict accidents before they happen.
Actively unblock and support team members, fostering a collaborative and efficient work environment.
Take a lead role in the ongoing maintenance of our Telematics systems, reducing tech debt and operating costs through sensible, data-driven design decisions.
Collaborate with product management and leadership across geos to define and execute ambitious roadmaps for Telematics.
Apply the latest AI tools to boost engineering and business productivity, sharing what you learn with the team.
Utilize your expertise in Python, AWS, Spark, SQL (Databricks/Presto), etc. to deliver robust and scalable solutions.
Participate in our team's on-call rotations, respond to incidents, and support other teams in mitigating customer-impacting events.

4+ years of software engineering industry experience
Experience in backend software development of large-scale distributed systems
Experience and/or interest in running large batch processing jobs with Spark or other large scale compute architectures
Experience and/or interest in Library development
Experience and/or interest in serving, versioning, monitoring ML models in production environments
Experience defining API schemas and developing backend services in a microservices environment
Experience with S3, Spark, Presto, Parquet, Databricks
You're a great communicator, and can advocate for your proposals while also empathizing with your cross-functional teammates' goals and priorities
You collaborate well with a geographically distributed team
Extended health and dental coverage options, along with life insurance and disability benefits

Device Identity and Access Organization
The Device Identity and Access organization is at the forefront of Okta’s Zero Trust vision. As a foundational pillar within Okta Research and Development (ORD), our mission is to transform the device itself into a secure, trusted, and effortless identity factor. We are the teams responsible for ensuring users can seamlessly interact with their work from any endpoint, anywhere in the world.
We engineer the end-to-end device experience—from our flagship FastPass , Okta Device Access (ODA), and Device Assurance . Our teams own the continuous authentication pipeline, device lifecycle management, and the sophisticated cloud services that analyze real-time trust and assurance signals to make frictionless, passwordless access a reality across Windows, macOS, iOS, Linux and Android.
Our organization is comprised of engineers who thrive at the intersection of deep client-side platform engineering and massive-scale distributed systems. The work we do secures millions of enterprise endpoints globally, prevents modern identity attacks, and fundamentally changes how people work by making world-class security completely invisible to the end user.
Explore our culture and technical innovations on the Okta Engineering Blog .
The Senior Software Engineer Opportunity
We seek a dynamic and influential Senior Software Engineer to join our Device Identity engineering team. The ideal candidate will leverage their deep Java experience to architect, build, and scale the critical server-side software and services at the heart of our security and identity platform. This is a high-visibility, hands-on opportunity to design solutions for current and emerging industry challenges.
You will not only demonstrate an aptitude for software engineering excellence but also act as a player-coach, mentoring other engineers and elevating the team's capabilities. You will join an engineering team that shares a passion for elegant solutions and believes in designing for scale, rigorous code reviews, automated testing, and an iterative process to build high-quality enterprise software.
What you’ll be doing
Drive cross-functional collaboration with Product, Design, and QA to ensure the seamless delivery of our most critical engineering initiatives.
Lead the design and implementation of new features and services within our core Java platform, taking ownership from conception to deployment.
Define and champion engineering best practices , and make critical contributions to technical designs, proposals, and long-term architectural decisions.
Mentor and coach other engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and by setting a high bar for quality and security.
Develop high-quality, maintainable software with comprehensive test coverage and drive improvements to our testing and CI/CD strategies.
Create and maintain high-quality technical documentation and foster a culture of knowledge sharing within the team and the broader organization.
Champion the adoption of AI-native engineering practices within our Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), utilizing AI coding assistants to accelerate delivery while ensuring rigorous security and code quality standards.

Expert knowledge of server-side technologies, including caching, asynchronous processing, and multi-threading.

Outschool’s mission is to inspire kids to love learning. In our fast-changing world, the traditional educational system struggles to meet the diverse and evolving needs of young learners. Outschool reimagines this system, offering flexible and engaging learning experiences as a supplement and alternative to traditional education. By connecting learners with a global community of teachers and peers through our online platform, we make learning personal, dynamic, and deeply human.
We've made significant strides since launching our marketplace of live online classes in 2017. Finding initial success with secular homeschoolers, we then expanded to enrichment learning to meet the needs of a wider audience, growing our business 16x since 2019.

Post-pandemic, we have evolved our platform to power academic learning, incorporated AI, and have begun to grow our international community. We're proud to have served over 1.5M passionate learners with more than $100M in annual bookings.
Driving disruptive, positive change in education is rewarding and hard. Outschool team members are encouraged to challenge themselves, take risks, and grow in their careers. We look for talented people whose sense of urgency, innate curiosity, and determination to drive impact will help Outschool achieve outsized results in pursuit of our mission.

We invite you to be part of an ambitious team dedicated to ensuring every learner can navigate the future with curiosity, resilience, and a love of learning.
Role
Outschool is looking for full-stack Software Engineers to develop and improve our suite of products to help parents, learners, and educators to engage in love of learning, all through an agentic-first development paradigm.

There is a wide variety of exciting and high-impact engineering challenges for the right candidate from smart UI to personalization to AI assistance to data optimization to tooling to platforms.

We’re hiring across levels - from early-career SWEs through senior architects - and will scope the role based on your experience, strengths, and the problems that inspire you and where you can have the biggest impacts.

Drive complex, high-impact engineering initiatives across a variety of product innovation areas
Partner closely with Product, Design, Data, and Engineering leadership to align on roadmap priorities, technical tradeoffs, risks, and execution strategy
Demonstrate AI-native development mindset leveraging fully agentic development workflows, while also contributing to establishing principles and best practices on AI development
For senior roles, mentor engineers and influence technical direction across teams through strong collaboration, communication, and domain expertise
Participate in standups, sprint planning, retros, production deployments, and on-call rotations

Professional software engineering experience; level will be determined based on experience and scope.
Proficiency in some of: TypeScript, React, Node.js, GraphQL, and PostgreSQL
Proven track record of both demonstrated proficiency in AI-native development, and leading teams into it
For senior roles, demonstrated technical leadership: you've set direction, made architectural calls, and raised the bar for a team
Strong communication and collaboration skills - you can translate technical complexity into clarity for engineers, product partners, and leadership alike

Experience in EdTech or building products for learners, educators, or families
Familiarity with search, discovery, personalization, AI, tooling, data insights, and/or payment systems
Background in marketplace technologies
Experience at a fast-paced startup or high-growth company

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.
At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
Why User Behavior?
You will build the backend systems that fundamentally shift how Roblox responds to unsafe behavior - from reactive, stateless punishment to a personalized, adaptive system that reflects who a user actually is.
You will own core backend infrastructure for a new capability at Roblox: a low-latency behavioral data layer, a centralized rules-and-inference engine, and a unified intervention-delivery framework that together let us treat users based on their real risk profile instead of a single point total. This is a rare opportunity to build foundational, high-scale systems that directly shape how Roblox understands and responds to risk across hundreds of millions of users.
You will feel a deep sense of responsibility building systems that directly affect millions of users, especially minors, on one of the world's largest platforms. Your work will reduce harm, improve fairness, and help ensure Roblox remains a place where creativity and community can thrive safely.

Build the User Behavior Foundation: Design and operate the low-latency, per-user behavioral data layer that powers real-time safety decisions - aggregating signals like violation history, in-game reports, and behavioral patterns into a single queryable source of truth.
Own the Consequence Engine: Build and evolve the centralized decision engine that combines deterministic rules with ML risk signals into a single, consistent safety decision the authoritative system every consequence flows through.
Own the Feature Restriction Platform: Build a unified, backend-driven framework for delivering safety interventions that any product team can plug into, replacing today's fragmented, feature-specific implementations.
Unify Abuse Reporting: Build the backend that consolidates reporting channels into a single, scalable framework - integrating LLM-based classification, agentic review workflows, and ML models to improve report routing, prioritization, and reporter feedback while meeting global regulatory requirements.
Design for trust and auditability: Build serving infrastructure that meets a high bar for explainability and fairness, since these systems directly determine consequences for millions of users.
Ship code, not just designs: Own end-to-end delivery - from system design through migration, testing, and production operation.

5+ years of experience building and operating production backend systems at scale, ideally in Go or a comparable statically-typed backend language.
Strong experience designing distributed systems: service APIs (RPC/gRPC), data modeling for high-throughput event ingestion, caching, and low-latency read paths.
Experience building and evolving rules engines, workflow/decision systems, or similarly stateful business-logic services.
Experience with streaming or batch data pipelines feeding a feature store or similar ingestion layer, and comfort partnering with ML engineers who consume that data.
Solid production operations fundamentals: monitoring, alerting, oncall, capacity planning, and incident response for systems with real user-facing impact.
Nice to have: experience in Trust & Safety, fraud, risk, or other adversarial domains; experience with feature stores or ML-serving infrastructure; experience building frontend-agnostic, backend-driven UI frameworks (e.g. server-driven intervention/notification rendering).

A Systems Thinker: capable of designing infrastructure that other teams (ML, feature teams, policy) build on top of, not just point solutions.
A Pragmatic Builder: scrappy and impact-oriented, comfortable turning scattered, undocumented signals and legacy code paths into clean, well-owned services.
Comfortable with Ambiguity: this space is actively being redefined — you'll help set the standard, not just implement one handed to you.
A Reliability-Minded Engineer: you treat testing, migrations, and oncall as first-class parts of the job, not afterthoughts.
Committed to Ethical, Responsible Engineering: dedicated to building systems that are fair, auditable, and operate with the utmost responsibility toward user safety.

s.t: HPC Systems Software Engineer – OpenCHAMI for Lugano or Zürich (professione segnalata)

Questo progetto, con sede di lavoro a Lugano o a Zurigo, si concentra sullo sviluppo e il potenziamento di OpenCHAMI per l’infrastruttura di supercalcolo di nuova generazione del CSCS. Il lavoro contribuirà alla creazione di un approccio aperto, scalabile e moderno alla gestione dei cluster per sistemi di calcolo ad alte prestazioni (HPC) su larga scala.
L’obiettivo principale è progettare, sviluppare, integrare e implementare funzionalità di OpenCHAMI su misura per i requisiti operativi dei supercomputer del CSCS.
Il progetto affronterà le sfide legate alla gestione di sistemi HPC e di intelligenza artificiale (AI) sempre più complessi e contribuirà all’evoluzione delle tecnologie open source di gestione dei cluster di nuova generazione.

Offriamo un contratto iniziale di due anni che ti darà l’opportunità di lavorare all’avanguardia nell’ambito delle infrastrutture HPC e di intelligenza artificiale presso il CSCS, contribuendo direttamente allo sviluppo di tecnologie che supporteranno i futuri sistemi di supercalcolo.
Avrai l’opportunità di contribuire a OpenCHAMI e alle relative iniziative open source, collaborando con la più ampia comunità HPC e partecipando a programmi di grande impatto sia a livello nazionale che internazionale, tra cui HPSF, OpenCHAMI e iniziative correlate.

Sviluppare e ampliare OpenCHAMI per soddisfare i requisiti operativi e di gestione dell’infrastruttura dei sistemi di supercalcolo attuali e di prossima generazione del CSCS.
Contribuire all’ecosistema open source di OpenCHAMI, compresi lo sviluppo, l’integrazione e l’evoluzione dei servizi e dei componenti correlati alla gestione dei cluster.
Sviluppare flussi di lavoro di automazione e gestione per migliorare il provisioning, la configurazione, il monitoraggio, la manutenzione e l’efficienza operativa dei sistemi su larga scala.
Collaborare strettamente con i team operativi HPC per comprendere i requisiti e le sfide operative e tradurli in soluzioni basate su OpenCHAMI robuste, scalabili e di facile manutenzione.
Contribuire all’architettura e all’evoluzione della piattaforma OpenCHAMI, garantendo che le soluzioni siano scalabili, affidabili, gestibili e allineate alle esigenze dei sistemi HPC e di IA su larga scala.
Partecipare attivamente ai flussi di lavoro di sviluppo open source, tra cui la progettazione del software, l’implementazione, i test, le revisioni del codice, il tracciamento dei problemi e le discussioni tecniche all’interno della comunità OpenCHAMI.
Collaborare con partner internazionali e con la più ampia comunità HPC per sviluppare e integrare soluzioni che promuovano la gestione dei cluster open source e l’automazione delle infrastrutture.
Redigere e aggiornare la documentazione tecnica, inclusi progetti di architettura, guide all’implementazione, procedure operative e best practice.
Valutare tecnologie e approcci emergenti rilevanti per la gestione delle infrastrutture HPC, l’osservabilità e l’automazione, e contribuire alla loro adozione ove opportuno.

Accogliamo con favore ingegneri con background diversi che siano desiderosi di contribuire alla nostra missione. Cerchiamo principalmente solide basi tecniche, un buon giudizio ingegneristico e la capacità di colmare le lacune tra i diversi ambiti. Curiosità, adattabilità, disponibilità ad apprendere sul campo e potenziale di crescita contano per noi più di una perfetta corrispondenza iniziale con i requisiti tecnici.

Einleitungstext
The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.
Projekthintergrund

This project with work location either Lugano or Zürich focuses on the development and advancement of OpenCHAMI for CSCS’s next-generation supercomputing infrastructure. The work will contribute to building an open, scalable, and modern approach to cluster management for large-scale High Performance Computing (HPC) systems.
The main objective is to design, develop, integrate, and deploy OpenCHAMI capabilities tailored to the operational requirements of CSCS supercomputers.
The project will address the challenges of managing increasingly complex HPC and AI systems and contribute to the evolution of next-generation open-source cluster management technologies.

We value technical excellence, curiosity, initiative, and the ability to learn and grow over a perfect checklist of skills. Working on next-generation HPC infrastructure requires a willingness to explore new technologies, tackle complex problems, and continuously develop new expertise.
If you are motivated to make a meaningful impact in this area but do not meet every requirement, we strongly encourage you to apply.

We offer an initially two-year contract providing the opportunity to work at the forefront of HPC and AI infrastructure at CSCS, contributing directly to the development of technologies that will support future supercomputing systems.
You will have the opportunity to contribute to OpenCHAMI and related open-source initiatives, collaborating with the broader HPC community and contributing to high-impact programs at both the national and international levels, including HPSF, OpenCHAMI, and related initiatives.
This is an opportunity to help shape how future CSCS supercomputers are managed, monitored, and operated, while contributing to open-source technologies with an impact well beyond a single system or institution.
Aufgaben-/Stellenbeschreibung
Develop and extend OpenCHAMI to meet the infrastructure management and operational requirements of CSCS’s current and next-generation supercomputing systems.
Contribute to the OpenCHAMI open-source ecosystem, including the development, integration, and evolution of related cluster management services and components.
Develop automation and management workflows to improve system provisioning, configuration, monitoring, maintenance, and operational efficiency at scale.
Collaborate closely with HPC operations teams to understand operational requirements and challenges, and translate them into robust, scalable, and maintainable OpenCHAMI-based solutions.
Contribute to the architecture and evolution of the OpenCHAMI platform, ensuring that solutions are scalable, reliable, maintainable, and aligned with the needs of large-scale HPC and AI systems.
Participate actively in open-source development workflows, including software design, implementation, testing, code reviews, issue tracking, and technical discussions within the OpenCHAMI community.

At Block, we strive to build the best financial products in the world. The Financial Platform Issuing team owns the card issuing platform that serves every Block brand — powering Cash App Card, the fourth-largest debit card program in the US, alongside Square Card and the new card programs Block launches next.
We run the full lifecycle of a card: issuance, fulfillment, and activation; real-time transaction authorization and processing across card networks; digital wallet provisioning; 3-D Secure authentication; clearing and settlement; and disputes. When a customer taps their card at a register, our systems decide the outcome in milliseconds, around the clock, in partnership with card networks and bank partners.
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Issuing server engineering team, you will bring deep card-network expertise to some of the most complex technical work on our roadmap. You will work alongside technical leads and cross functional teams, going deep where our platform meets the networks: specifications, protocols, certification, mandates, conformance, and production behavior.
This is a hands-on role. You will build systems and tooling, debug at the message level, and turn your network expertise into durable capabilities that other engineers can use. You will also work directly with the networks themselves — not only understanding what they require, but knowing where and how to influence outcomes for Block.
You Will
Be a deep technical expert on global card networks, helping Issuing teams interpret network specifications, message flows, certification requirements, mandates, and production behavior — and working directly with the networks to influence requirements, resolve ambiguity, and secure outcomes that matter for Block.
Lead complex, ambiguous engineering problems at the network boundary that span multiple teams, systems, or domains.
Partner with technical leads, program DRIs, and senior stakeholders to shape solutions where card-network requirements intersect with Block's issuing platform.
Stay deeply hands-on: write production code, build certification and conformance tooling, analyze network messages, review designs and code, and debug issues down to the protocol and field level.
Drive network certification and mandatory release cycles end to end, and translate network requirements into clear, pragmatic engineering decisions.
Establish shared frameworks, standards, tooling, and practices that make network expertise durable and enable teams to operate independently.
Raise the technical capability of engineers around you through design guidance, code reviews, mentorship, documentation, and clear technical judgment.
Apply AI-powered tools throughout the engineering lifecycle to improve velocity and quality, and help establish effective patterns for broader team use.
Share operational ownership of critical financial systems through on-call, incident response, and continuous improvements to reliability and correctness.
You Have
Deep, current expertise with at least one major card network, ideally Visa, including direct connectivity, ISO 8583, authorization and clearing flows, stand-in processing, specifications, certification, and mandate cycles.
Personally built, certified, or operated a live direct network connection — not only integrated through a processor.
Experience working directly with card networks to land concrete outcomes, such as rulings, exceptions, extensions, configuration changes, defect fixes, or certification outcomes.
Strong hands-on software engineering experience building and operating highly reliable financial or payments systems at scale.
A track record of leading technically complex, ambiguous work across team boundaries and influencing technical direction beyond your immediate area of ownership.
Experience creating durable technical leverage — frameworks, standards, tooling, architecture, or practices that other engineers and teams adopt.
Broad understanding of the card lifecycle, with depth in areas such as issuance and fulfillment, provisioning and activation, authorization, ledgering, clearing and settlement, reconciliation, disputes, or fraud.
Working knowledge of Mastercard and American Express, alongside deep expertise in at least one major network.
Fluency with AI-assisted engineering workflows and sound judgment in evaluating and applying AI-generated output.
Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation for critical financial systems.

Husky is what we call the distributed, petabyte-scale columnar event store at the heart of our Event Platform, which powers dozens of Datadog’s most popular products – Logs, RUM, APM, Cloud Network Monitoring, Netflow, and many more. Husky was built from the ground up at Datadog to store and query massive volumes of event data at low cost, with data fully queryable within seconds of arrival.
As a Senior Software Engineer on this team, you'll work hands-on with a distributed storage system at petabyte scale, and help us evolve our platform to support the next level of scale that will power the AI era.

We will move from a custom storage format towards open standards (Parquet, Arrow, DataFusion) enabling on prem solutions, increasingly complex analytical/batch workloads, and powering AI observability, sustainably into the future.

You'll partner closely with Husky Ingestion, Metadata, and Platform, and increasingly with Lakehouse on the Iceberg-compatible boundary between Husky and analytical/batch workloads. You will also work with the open source community to build the next generation of reusable software solutions that can be operated at scale.
Datadog has a culture that is increasingly rare in mature technology companies. We are an engineering driven, bottom up, high agency/high responsibility culture–where everyone is empowered and expected to drive the technological and strategic direction of the business over time.

We are a blameless culture where we believe supporting each other through challenges produces the best outcomes over time and our track record corroborates this. We are open source champions.

We believe in the flexibility of working remotely but also the value of bringing people together across our various offices worldwide–and our offices are nice places to work.

Drive Husky to the next level of adoption by migrating our storage format to open source Parquet and re-imagine compaction on a format-agnostic, DataFusion-based substrate
Drive concrete cost-reduction work: block-level inverted index compression, combining the database with external objects at the row level, and storage tiering/caching
Scale our solution to enable customers to manage event versioning at scale, using temporal-database techniques.
Play an influential role in operating and deciding how to best operate our service going forward.
Work across the write path (with Ingestion) and toward a cleaner Iceberg-based handoff to ADP/Lakehouse for batch/analytical workloads

Enthusiastic and experienced with large-scale distributed systems and/or storage engines
Comfortable with improving and operating large distributed systems that customers rely on for critical business functions
Strong fundamentals in columnar/file storage formats (Parquet, ORC, Arrow) or comparable systems
Bonus : experience with Go, Java, or Rust; with compaction or compression/encoding schemes (RLE, dictionary, delta, gorilla); with object storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) at scale, including caching and cost optimization; with Kafka and stream processing; or with Kubernetes

AI frameworks like LangChain, LlamaIndex, and n8n are quickly becoming the default way developers build with AI — and MongoDB wants to be the data platform that shows up everywhere they build. As part of the AI Builders Experience (ABX) org, we're standing up a brand new engineering team in Gurugram to make that happen, and we're looking for Software Engineers to be among its founding members.
The team owns the connective layer between MongoDB and third-party AI frameworks, platforms, and tools — the integrations that let developers use MongoDB effectively with the AI stack they've already chosen. That means shipping into some of the fastest-moving open-source ecosystems in tech, working mostly in Python and TypeScript, and partnering with the Database Experience (DBX) org when an integration needs new driver, platform, or product capability underneath it.
This is a strong role for an engineer who wants to grow into the AI space with real ownership. You'll own well-scoped projects from design through release, work with fast-moving and sometimes unproven technologies, and get a clear view of how the ecosystem is evolving.

Priorities shift as frameworks change and customer demand moves, so we're looking for engineers who are adaptable, ask good questions, and take pride in shipping.

Much of your work will happen in public: sending pull requests to upstream repositories, working through external maintainer review cycles, and participating in developer communities as MongoDB.
You'll work closest with the engineers sitting next to you, pairing on hard problems, reviewing each other's code, and dividing up a broad portfolio, with senior engineers and your manager close at hand as you take on larger pieces of it.
MongoDB engineering teams pride themselves on building high-quality software and living our cultural values every day. We value intellectual curiosity, intellectual honesty, customer empathy, and building together in an environment that prioritizes collaboration over competition.
We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Gurugram for our hybrid working model.
Position expectations
Build, test, and ship MongoDB integrations across a broad AI framework ecosystem that includes technologies like LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, n8n, and Mastra
Own well-scoped projects end to end on weekly-to-quarterly timelines, taking responsibility for the scope, schedule, and quality of your own work and communicating progress and trade-offs clearly
Solve day-to-day technical problems with growing independence, using the team's established patterns and past practice to guide your decisions, and seeking guidance on non-standard problems
Contribute to exploratory work on new frameworks: help evaluate an integration's feasibility, build a first working version of the piece you own, and share what you learn with the team
Contribute high-quality code upstream to repositories MongoDB doesn't own, following the team's contribution practices and maintaining a high standard of professionalism and courtesy through external maintainer review cycles
Work within and improve the team's engineering practices: CI/CD, automated testing across framework and server versions, version compatibility checks, and release steps. Suggest improvements where you see repeated friction
Help keep the integrations you work on healthy: monitor for upstream breaking changes, handle upgrades, triage incoming issues, and follow through after release
Coordinate with adjacent teams, including DBX, when your work depends on driver, platform, or product capability, and escalate cross-team dependencies and risks early rather than working around them

Description de l'entreprise
Swiss Medical Network est l'un des groupes de cliniques privées les plus importants de Suisse. Il s'est fixé pour objectif d'offrir des soins médicaux de premier ordre à ses patients suisses et étrangers.

Swiss Medical Network convainc par la haute qualité de ses prestations, un environnement de travail agréable et une équipe de direction expérimentée à l'esprit entrepreneurial. Le réseau exploite actuellement 21 cliniques et hôpitaux dans toute la Suisse et est présent dans les trois principales régions linguistiques.
Description du poste
En tant que Fullstack Developer (AI \& Digital Health), vous jouez un rôle moteur dans la transformation numérique de nos cliniques. Vous concevez et développez des solutions logicielles innovantes assistées par l'IA, qui améliorent le parcours du patient tout en soulageant le personnel médical. Vous agissez comme un pont technique entre les exigences médicales et les technologies de pointe, garantissant que nos applications de santé numériques sont sécurisées, évolutives et conviviales.

Votre domaine d'activité
Développement \& Architecture de solutions : Conception et implémentation d'applications web Fullstack évolutives (Frontend \& Backend) pour un usage clinique et administratif.
Intégration de l'IA : Développement et intégration de modèles d'apprentissage automatique (Machine Learning), de LLM (Large Language Models) et de services d'IA déterministes (explainable AI) dans des applications existantes et nouvelles pour soutenir les processus diagnostiques ou administratifs.
Données \& Interfaces : Connexion des applications aux systèmes primaires cliniques (KIS/HIS/DPI) en utilisant des standards d'interopérabilité modernes (ex. FHIR, HL7\) et garantie d'un échange de données fluide.
Security by Design : Garantie des standards de sécurité les plus élevés et de la conformité à la protection des données (LPD/RGPD) lors du traitement des données sensibles des patients, en étroite coordination avec le délégué à la protection des données.
DevOps \& Cloud : Mise en place et maintenance de pipelines CI/CD ainsi que gestion de l'infrastructure Cloud pour l'exploitation des solutions d'IA.
Prototyping : Développement rapide de preuves de concept (PoC) pour évaluer le potentiel des nouvelles technologies d'IA pour le quotidien clinique et les rendre tangibles.
Collaboration : Étroite coopération avec les Data Scientists, les médecins et le personnel soignant afin de créer des solutions centrées sur l'utilisateur ("User Centricity").
Votre profil
Formation : Diplôme universitaire en informatique, ingénierie logicielle ou qualification comparable avec un fort accent sur les technologies web modernes.
Compétences en développement : Expérience approfondie dans les frameworks Backend (ex. Python, , Java) et Frontend (ex. React, Angular, modernes, idéalement sur la Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Looker). Des connaissances en Python sont privilégiées en raison de l'orientation IA.
Expertise en IA : Expérience pratique dans l'intégration de composants IA/ML (ex. API OpenAI, LangChain, Hugging Face, TensorFlow) dans des environnements logiciels productifs.
Secteur de la santé : Une expérience avec les normes du secteur de la santé (FHIR, HL7, DICOM) est un avantage, mais pas obligatoire si vous êtes prêt à vous y former. Une expérience avec le "Software as Medical Device" et les processus de certification correspondants constitue un atout majeur.
Méthode de travail : Un mode de travail autonome, agile (Scrum/Kanban) et orienté solutions. Vous avez une mentalité "Can\-Do" et prenez plaisir à résoudre des problèmes complexes par le code.
Personnalité : Esprit d'innovation couplé à une conscience de la qualité. Vous savez rendre des sujets techniques compréhensibles pour des interlocuteurs non techniques.
Langues : De langue maternelle allemande avec un niveau courant/négociation en français (ou inversement) ; de bonnes connaissances en anglais sont requises pour la collaboration au sein de nos équipes linguistiques régionales.
Tech\-Stack : Des connaissances en technologies de conteneurisation (Docker, Kubernetes), plateformes Cloud (Azure/GCP) et gestion de versions (Git) sont prérequis.
Informations supplémentaires
Notre offre
Innovation : Nous vous offrons la possibilité de travailler à la pointe de l'innovation médicale et de développer des solutions d'IA qui apportent une véritable plus\-value à la vie des patients.
Création : Vous bénéficiez d'une grande marge de manœuvre technique dans un environnement dynamique qui favorise les circuits de décision courts et la pensée entrepreneuriale.
Environnement : Un climat de travail inspirant au sein d'une équipe interdisciplinaire composée de médecins et de spécialistes IT, un package salarial attractif ainsi que des prestations sociales progressistes vous attendent.
Développement : Réjouissez\-vous de projets passionnants avec les dernières technologies et une grande responsabilité personnelle au sein d'un groupe de cliniques en pleine croissance.

Grove Collaborative is a sustainability-focused consumer products company creating household and personal care essentials that are effective, beautifully designed, and healthier for people and the planet. We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.
Engineering at Grove
The Grove product, engineering, and design team is rooted in a data and goal-driven culture. We take ownership of big business and technology challenges and solve them quickly and robustly. We operate in small, autonomous teams, build on a modern and evolving stack, and deploy frequently to deliver value to the business as fast as possible. We value trust, collaboration, and shared ownership.
About the Opportunity
We’re looking for a senior engineer whose center of gravity is the front end, but who follows a problem wherever it goes — into an API, a data model, a third-party integration, a build pipeline.
We care far more about how you think than about which frameworks are on your resume. Our storefront runs on Shopify today, and parts of it won’t tomorrow. The stack has changed before and will change again. What we need is someone who can walk into unfamiliar territory, figure out how it actually works, and make a good call about it.
This isn’t a role for someone waiting to be told what to build. We want a true self-starter: endlessly curious, genuinely ambitious, and humble enough to be trusted with real influence.
You’ll lead projects end to end — shaping the problem with product and design, collaborating with other engineers on the approach, making the architectural calls, shipping, and then looking at what the numbers say.
To be clear about scope: this is a senior individual contributor role. You’ll lead projects but you won’t be managing people or owning org-wide technical strategy. You’ll be in the code.
What You’ll Own
Project leadership — Lead front end and full stack initiatives from ambiguous problem statement to shipped, measured outcome. Make the architecture calls, sequence the work, and keep the project honest about tradeoffs.
Product and design partnership — Work shoulder to shoulder with product managers and designers. We expect you to have opinions about the experience itself, not just how to build what you were handed.
Craft, performance, and quality — Own performance, stability, accessibility, and maintainability in the code you and your team ship, at the scale Grove actually runs at.
Ecosystem integration — Partner across our third-party ecosystem — mobile apps, subscription services, analytics, search and discovery, loyalty — to build experiences that feel like one product instead of six vendors.
AI-assisted development — Use AI tooling aggressively as a force multiplier, and hold the line on quality while you do it. More on this below.
Design system — Partner with UX Design to define and scale our design system and UI component library.
Measurement — Work with analytics partners to make sure the tracking exists to tell you whether what you shipped actually worked.
Best practices — Champion testing, documentation, and workflows the rest of the team can build on.

7+ years building and operating production web applications, with the front end as your strongest area.
Deep expertise in JavaScript and TypeScript, at least one modern component framework (React, Vue, Svelte, or similar), state management, and performance optimization for consumer-facing applications.
Genuinely comfortable working across the stack — APIs, data models, integrations, CI, the browser, and the boring infrastructure in between.
New technology doesn’t scare you. You’ve been dropped into an unfamiliar framework, language, or platform and gotten productive fast, and you can point to a time you did it. You evaluate new tools on the merits instead of defaulting to what you already know or chasing whatever is new.
You’re honest about what you don’t know. You can say “I haven’t worked with that” without flinching, and you don’t paper over the gap with a confident guess.
You lead projects, not just tickets. You’ve taken something vague, made it concrete, brought other people along, and shipped it.
You think like a designer and a product person. You notice when a flow is confusing, you push back when a spec doesn’t make sense for the customer, and you can tell the difference between polish that matters and polish that doesn’t.
You work well with others. You give direct feedback kindly, you take it well, and people want you on their project.
A real sense of ownership and pride in the experiences you ship and the code you leave behind.
You write things down, and people understand them. You can walk a PM or a designer through a technical tradeoff without hiding behind jargon, and the decisions you make stay legible to whoever picks up the code six months later.
Genuine enthusiasm for Grove’s mission and sustainability values, not just the tech stack.
How We Work Together
This is a high trust environment. You’ll get real scope and real decisions early, and nobody is going to look over your shoulder while you do the work. Trust runs both directions: we’ll be straight with you about the business, the tradeoffs, and the parts of the codebase we aren’t proud of, and we expect that same candor back.
We value psychological safety first and foremost. It’s the precondition for everything else on this list. The teams that solve genuinely hard problems are the ones where people feel safe saying “I don’t understand this yet.”
“I haven’t worked with that” is a complete answer here. We have deep respect for an engineer who names the edge of their own knowledge instead of bluffing past it. We don’t need you to know everything. We need you to be honest about where your expertise begins and ends — and that honesty is worth more to us than a confident guess, in an interview and on the job.
How We think About AI
We’re serious about this, so we’d rather be direct than let you find out later.
AI tooling is part of how this team works every day, not an experiment on the side. We want someone who genuinely enjoys these tools and keeps getting better with them.
Nobody here has AI figured out, and we’re skeptical of anyone who says they do. The tooling changes month to month. We are all working it out together, in the open. We’d rather hire someone actively learning than someone with a methodology to evangelize.
We’re looking for someone whose judgment stays their own. You should be able to read what a model produced, disagree with it, and explain why — about architecture, about correctness, about whether the thing should be built at all.
The version of this we don’t want: code that ships because a model was confident. If you can’t explain why your code looks the way it does, “the model wrote it” isn’t an answer.
The version we do want: someone who moves twice as fast with these tools and whose standards didn’t move at all.
This is where honesty about the edges of your knowledge matters most. AI makes it effortless to produce work you don’t actually understand. Flagging that is a strength here, not an admission.
